$comment: CWE -> canonical remediation pattern catalog for the Fix Strategist agent. Keep entries factual and generic (framework-level guidance), not tied to one file in this repo — the Strategist applies the pattern to the specific defect site. See catalog/README.md for the entry contract and how to add a CWE.

CWE-943.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL/SQL Injection)
CWE-943.applicable_when: User-controlled input is concatenated into a query string or query document (SQL, JPQL, MongoDB BasicQuery/JSON) instead of being bound as a parameter, letting the caller inject query operators or structure rather than only values.
CWE-943.canonical_approach: Replace string concatenation with parameterised criteria. For Spring Data MongoDB, use the Criteria API (Criteria.where(field).is(value), .regex(Pattern.quote(value)) for literal substring search) or a derived repository method (findByNameContaining...) instead of building a BasicQuery from a StringBuilder. For JPA/SQL, use named or positional bind parameters, never string-built JPQL/SQL. Never rely on escaping or blacklisting characters as the primary defence.
anti_patterns: Escaping or blacklisting specific characters (quotes, braces) instead of parameterising the query
Wrapping the same concatenation in a try/catch or adding a length limit without changing the query construction
Validating input format client-side only, with no server-side change to the sink

CWE-89.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command (SQL Injection)
CWE-89.applicable_when: User-controlled input is concatenated into a SQL string executed via Statement, string-built JPQL, or a native query, instead of being bound as a parameter.
CWE-89.canonical_approach: Use PreparedStatement with bind parameters, or JPA/Hibernate named parameters (:param) — never String.format or '+' concatenation into query text. For dynamic filtering, use the Criteria API / Specification pattern rather than building SQL text.
anti_patterns: Escaping quotes manually instead of using bind parameters
Building the WHERE clause by string concatenation even when values are eventually escaped
references: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

CWE-306.title: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-306.applicable_when: An endpoint that reads or mutates sensitive data (PII, payroll, credentials) has no authentication requirement — any network caller can invoke it directly.
CWE-306.canonical_approach: Require authentication on the endpoint via the framework's security layer (Spring Security filter chain / method security, e.g. @PreAuthorize, or a gateway-level auth requirement) rather than an ad-hoc check inside the handler. Prefer denying by default and allow-listing the few endpoints that must stay public (health checks), instead of allow-listing which endpoints need auth.
anti_patterns: Checking a hardcoded header or shared secret inside the controller method instead of using the security framework
Adding authentication only to the specific endpoint named in the issue while leaving structurally identical sibling endpoints open
references: OWASP Top 10 A01:2021 - Broken Access Control

CWE-284.title: Improper Access Control
CWE-284.applicable_when: A resource is reachable by a caller who should not have that level of access — broader than pure authentication, includes missing authorization/role checks once a caller is identified.
CWE-284.canonical_approach: Enforce authorization at the same layer as authentication (method security or gateway policy), scoped to the specific role/permission the operation requires, and verified with a negative test (a caller without the role gets 403, not 200 with filtered data).
anti_patterns: Filtering the response after the fact instead of denying the request
Trusting a client-supplied role/ID field instead of the authenticated principal

CWE-532.title: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
CWE-532.owasp: A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
CWE-532.applicable_when: Request/response bodies, exception messages, or entity objects containing PII, credentials or payroll data are passed directly to a logger (log.info(request), log.debug(entity), or a logging interceptor that dumps full payloads).
CWE-532.canonical_approach: Log identifiers (e.g. employee ID, request ID) instead of full objects. Where a payload must be logged for diagnostics, mask or redact the sensitive fields before logging, or gate verbose payload logging behind a debug flag that is off in production. Never log raw exception objects that may embed request data in their message.
anti_patterns: Lowering only the log level (e.g. from INFO to DEBUG) without removing the sensitive fields
Redacting in a toString() override that a different log call bypasses

CWE-200.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
CWE-200.applicable_when: A response body (directly or via a shared DTO/entity) includes fields the caller should not see — e.g. salary or payroll fields returned to any caller of a general-purpose read endpoint.
CWE-200.canonical_approach: Introduce a response DTO scoped to what the endpoint's caller is entitled to see, instead of serialising the persistence entity directly. Combine with the relevant authorization pattern (CWE-306/CWE-284) so the restriction cannot be bypassed by calling the endpoint without the expected role.
anti_patterns: Adding @JsonIgnore to the entity field, which then hides it from every consumer that legitimately needs it
Filtering fields in the frontend/client instead of the server response

CWE-770.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
CWE-770.applicable_when: A handler or scheduled job loads an entire collection or result set into memory with no pagination, page size cap, or streaming (e.g. repository.findAll() over an unbounded MongoDB collection), letting the size of the request cost scale with the size of the data.
CWE-770.canonical_approach: Replace the unbounded read with a paginated query (Spring Data's Pageable / Page<T>) with a server-enforced maximum page size, or a streaming query (Stream<T> with @QueryHints for cursor-based reads) for jobs that must touch every record. Callers that need 'all' data should page through it rather than the server materialising it in one response.
anti_patterns: Adding a query parameter for page size that the server does not cap, so a caller can still request an unbounded page
Fixing the endpoint but leaving an equivalent unbounded call reachable from a scheduled job

CWE-400.title: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
CWE-400.applicable_when: An operation's cost (CPU, memory, DB load) is controlled by caller-supplied input with no upper bound — unanchored regex, unbounded recursion, or an unbounded fan-out of downstream calls per request.
CWE-400.canonical_approach: Bound the cost of the operation server-side: cap input length/complexity before it reaches the expensive operation, use Pattern.quote()/anchored patterns for user-supplied regex fragments, and add explicit limits (max page size, max fan-out, timeouts on downstream calls).
anti_patterns: Relying on a client-side limit that the server does not itself enforce
Catching the resulting timeout/OOM instead of bounding the cause

CWE-798.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
CWE-798.applicable_when: A password, API key, or connection secret is present as a literal in source (application.properties committed with a real value, a string constant, a default fallback in code) rather than injected from the environment or a secret store.
CWE-798.canonical_approach: Move the credential to an externalised source (environment variable, Spring Cloud Config encrypted property, or a secret manager) and fail fast at startup if it is absent, rather than falling back to a hardcoded default. Rotate the exposed credential once removed from source.
anti_patterns: Moving the literal into a 'default' properties file that still ships in the build artifact
Leaving the hardcoded value as a commented-out fallback

CWE-1104.title: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
CWE-1104.applicable_when: A pom.xml (or other manifest) pins a third-party library to a version with a publicly known vulnerability advisory, whether that pin is explicit or resolved via the parent's dependency management, and no newer, non-vulnerable version is actually in use.
CWE-1104.canonical_approach: Identify the minimum version that remediates the specific advisory (not blindly 'latest', which can introduce unrelated breaking changes outside this fix's scope) by reading the advisory's own affected/fixed version range. Pin that version explicitly if it is not already. Rebuild and confirm via `mvn dependency:tree` that the *resolved* version in the dependency tree actually reflects the bump — a `<version>` edit can be textually correct and still not take effect if another dependency management entry overrides it.
anti_patterns: Bumping to whatever 'latest' resolves to without checking the advisory's actual fixed-version boundary, or without checking it doesn't pull in unrelated breaking changes
Editing a version only in a `<properties>` variable when a separate explicit `<version>` tag elsewhere in the same or a child module overrides it, so the resolved version never actually changes
Suppressing or ignoring the finding (a dependency-check allowlist/ignore rule) instead of upgrading the library
Verifying only that the pom.xml text changed, without confirming the resolved dependency tree reflects the new version
references: OWASP Top 10 A06:2021 - Vulnerable and Outdated Components

CWE-79.title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)
CWE-79.applicable_when: User-controlled input is written into an HTML response, a template, or a client-rendered field without contextual output encoding.
CWE-79.canonical_approach: Use the templating engine's default auto-escaping (do not mark tainted values as safe/unescaped) for HTML contexts, and apply the correct encoder for the output context (HTML body, attribute, URL, JS string) when auto-escaping is bypassed for a legitimate reason.
anti_patterns: Blacklisting <script> tags instead of encoding on output
Escaping on input/storage instead of on output, which breaks legitimate data and still misses some contexts
